domainLookupsHint: Checks contacts' domain proofs. The resolver sees which domain.
domainLookupsInfo: Uses {{name}}; if it fails, Quad9, Cloudflare or Google. It never sees your chats. A proof on a website shows that site your IP address.
hyperdhtHint: Optional fallback when WebRTC fails. Empty: WebRTC only.
hyperdhtInfo: Lets chats use HyperDHT from this browser. The relay forwards encrypted bytes: it sees your address and when you talk, never what you say.
irohHint: Used when WebRTC cannot connect. One per line, up to four.
irohInfo: A browser cannot send Iroh's UDP packets, so Iroh chats here use a relay. It sees which devices talk and when, never what they say.
irohInfoDirect: Iroh connects directly when it can, through a relay when it cannot. A relay sees which devices talk and when, never what they say.
pushRelayHint: For waking contacts from a browser. Empty: none.
pushRelayInfo: A browser cannot post to a push service; this relay does. It sees your IP address and when you wake someone, never the message.
readRelaysHint: Finds a first contact sooner. Relays see which keys it looks up.
readRelaysInfo: This app reads the Mainline DHT directly. On: it also asks the Pkarr relays below. If the DHT is blocked, it asks them anyway.
relaysHint: One per line. They only see signed, encrypted packets.
relaysInfoDirect: Contacts on the web and in the extension cannot reach the Mainline DHT and read through relays, so this app writes to them too.
relaysInfoWeb: Browsers cannot reach the Mainline DHT, so relays do it for them. They never carry your messages, calls or services. Every relay listed is used.
title: Network
turnCredentialAgain: Enter the credential again: backups leave it out.
turnHint: Optional. Used only when a direct connection fails.
turnInfo: It forwards encrypted WebRTC packets. It is connectivity infrastructure, not a Ghostly server.
